articles.headline: Does Elon Musk have too much influence in space?
Tesla Robotaxi Rollout Faces Fresh Scrutiny
articles.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) is facing fresh questions about its robotaxi rollout after a Bloomberg test in Austin showed long waits, booking issues and a very small operating fleet.
Over the past few weeks, a Bloomberg reporter said some Tesla robotaxi rides came with wait times as long as 30 minutes, while there were also periods when bookings were unavailable. In one case, a robotaxi arrived for pickup but failed to start, telling the rider to contact customer support. Pickups and drop-offs were also uneven, with the rider sometimes forced to walk several buildings away despite closer open spots.
The bigger issue is scale. Bloomberg's review of public filings found Tesla has only 59 vehicles in its Austin robotaxi fleet. That makes the service look more limited than the larger rollout many investors had hoped for.
CFRA analyst Garrett Nelson said the fleet size is well below the firm's already bearish expectations, adding that Elon Musk has overpromised for more than a decade. For investors, the next test is whether Tesla can quickly improve availability, reliability and fleet size in Austin.

articles.headline: Brace for SpaceX's stock to show 'extreme' volatility, a bullish analyst warns
articles.text:
Brace for SpaceX’s stock to show ‘extreme’ volatility, a bullish analyst warns
Early analyst coverage of SpaceX’s stock is starting to roll in now that the IPO is imminent
SpaceX is on the cusp of becoming a public company, more than 24 years after Elon Musk founded the rocket maker. And while it will be several weeks before analysts at the biggest banks are able to weigh in with views on the stock, those at firms uninvolved in the initial public offering are already starting to give their opinions.
“We believe that SpaceX will use its expertise in engineering, manufacturing and space technologies to grow to the largest communications, cloud/AI company in the world,” Oppenheimer analysts led by Timothy Horan said in a note to clients on Thursday as they initiated coverage on SpaceX SPCX.

articles.headline: Big Tech stocks mostly fall, with Alphabet and Microsoft posting sharp losses
articles.text:
1 hour ago
Big Tech stocks mostly fall, with Alphabet and Microsoft posting sharp losses
Big Tech stocks were mostly struggling Thursday, with Google parent Alphabet and Microsoft posting sharp drops exceeding 2%.
The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF — an exchange-traded fund that holds seven Big Tech stocks, including Nvidia, Apple, Google parent Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon.com and Facebook parent Meta Platforms — was down 0.7%. Tesla and Nvidia were the only two stocks in the fund’s portfolio posting gains, according to FactSet data, at last check.
Alphabet and Microsoft had the largest losses. Shares of Alphabet were down 2.4% late morning Thursday, while Microsoft slid 2.2%. Although Big Tech stocks have an outsized weighting in the S&P 500, the index was up 0.4% as most of its sectors were rising Thursday.
